name: StartPOSend
caption: Start sending purchase order

configuration.description: SmartField reference to the purchase order (table 38), written as exactly one placeholder, e.g. "{{trigger_PurchaseHeader}}" or the current record of a For Each. Resolved like Modify Record's reference: an undotted name is looked up in the flow context, a dotted path is walked through the SmartField definitions.

outputs.name: FlowsQueued
outputs.when: always - number of flows queued, as an invariant integer ('0' when no flow is published on the trigger)

rules.message: Please fill in the highlighted fields.

rules.check: The resolved record is not a Purchase Header (table 38), or its Document Type is not Order (a quote is not sent).
rules.message: The record of "%1" must be a purchase order.

rules.check: No flow (other than the calling one) is published on POSent; nothing is queued, FlowsQueued = 0, an Info entry is logged and the flow continues.
rules.message: No flow is published for "%1" - nothing was started.

notes: Requires the AutoFlow Supplier Foundation app. See docs/apps/SupplierFoundation.md.
Offered in the step picker for every trigger.

Fire and forget: queues every flow published on POSent (5564016) for the record, with the outputs the page action 'Send to supplier' would give them, each as its own execution with a Job Queue entry. The calling flow continues at once and never learns how the runs end.
The calling flow itself is never queued (so a flow on that trigger cannot start itself over and over). Two flows that start each other's triggers are not guarded.

Business Central starts a Job Queue entry only after the transaction that created it commits. In a background flow that is the end of this step; in an inline or synchronous flow it is the end of the caller's transaction, and if that transaction rolls back, nothing is started.
Logs an Info entry '%1 flow(s) started for %2.'
The page action follows its runs in a progress window; this step does not. Typical use: a flow on When a document is released (Purchase Header) that sends the order.
